---
name: hub-design-decision-management
description: Create and maintain feature specs (FEAT), significant change proposals (RFC), versioned architecture or model designs (DES), and decision records (ADR). Use for feature planning, design alternatives, harness architecture versions, choosing implementation strategies, or superseding prior technical decisions.
---

# Design & Decision Management

**Scope:** One workflow for requirements → proposals/designs → architectural choices. For indexing and sync use `hub-docs-governance`; for measured comparisons use `hub-experiment-evaluation`.

## Select the *minimum* record needed

| Record | Trigger | Path |
|---|---|---|
| `FEAT` | Durable, observable capability and testable acceptance criteria | `docs/features/FEAT-0001-slug.md` |
| `RFC` | Significant change needs review/consensus | `docs/proposals/RFC-0001-slug.md` |
| `DES` | Detailed design or a meaningful competing design version | `docs/designs/DES-0001-slug/{README.md,v1.md,...}` |
| `ADR` | Consequential choice and rationale, including reversal | `docs/decisions/ADR-0001-slug.md` |

Avoid creating all four for minor changes. Use existing IDs for revisions to the same feature/design; allocate a **new ID** for each independent RFC or ADR. Minor wording edits stay in Git history.

## Procedure

1. **Inspect first:** `docs/README.md`, living architecture, previous versions, relevant code/tests and tracked issues/experiments. Distinguish intended design from implemented reality.
2. **Define problem:** users/stakeholders, goals, non-goals, constraints and alternatives; link existing records instead of duplicating their contents.
3. **Document in the correct record:**
   - **FEAT:** contract, edge/failure cases, permissions, measurable acceptance criteria; mark `proposed`, `in-development`, `released`, or `deprecated` using evidence.
   - **RFC:** motivation, proposal, alternatives, roll-out, open questions; status `draft`, `in-review`, `accepted`, or `rejected`.
   - **DES:** components/interfaces, state/control flow, error/retry/security/observability, trade-offs and evaluation plan; use `vN.md` snapshots **only for materially different designs**. Preserve prior version and index versions in the design `README.md` with status, evidence and implementation links.
   - **ADR:** context/decision drivers, specific choice, serious alternatives, consequences and evidence; status `proposed` or `accepted` until formally superseded or deprecated.
4. **Link relationships:** `FEAT` ↔ `RFC` ↔ `DES-xxxx@vN` ↔ `EXP/EVAL` ↔ `ADR` ↔ PR/commit/release, where applicable.
5. **Version/supersede correctly:** A new design alternative gets `DES-xxxx@v(N+1)` and a delta explanation. An overturned architectural decision gets a **new ADR ID** with `supersedes: ADR-xxxx`; set `superseded_by` on the previous ADR. Do not rewrite historical decisions.
6. **Update the index** and affected living docs **only when implementation is verified**. An accepted RFC, selected DES and accepted ADR do not prove code is shipped.

## Reusable compact templates

### Framework-first architecture documents

For a living architecture document or a DES snapshot that models a complete system, use the [framework-first architecture template](references/framework-architecture-template.md). It complements the compact record templates below with a system, framework, object model, and runtime-flow structure.


### FEAT — feature contract

```markdown
---
id: FEAT-0001
title: Agent approval
status: proposed
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
related: [DES-0001]
---
# FEAT-0001 — Agent approval
## User problem / goals and non-goals
## Required behavior (including failure/permission cases)
## Acceptance criteria (Given / When / Then)
## Dependencies / UX or API links
## Implementation evidence (tests, PR, commit, release; pending until verified)
```

### RFC — significant proposal

```markdown
---
id: RFC-0001
title: New task scheduler
status: draft
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
related: [DES-0001]
---
# RFC-0001 — New task scheduler
## Motivation and constraints
## Proposed change
## Alternatives / trade-offs
## Compatibility / migration
## Evaluation and open questions
## Review outcome (only when decided)
```

### DES — design snapshot + index

```markdown
---
id: DES-0001
title: Harness execution
version: 2
status: proposed
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
supersedes: DES-0001@v1
related: [RFC-0001, EXP-0001]
---
# DES-0001@v2 — Harness execution
## Problem / scope / requirements
## Architecture: components, interfaces, state, control flow
## Failure, security, observability, operational trade-offs
## Difference from v1 and alternatives
## Evaluation plan and success criteria
## Implementation / migration plan and open questions
```

In `docs/designs/DES-0001-slug/README.md` maintain:

```markdown
| Version | Status | Key difference | Evidence | Implementation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [v1](v1.md) | implemented | sequential | EXP-0001 | commit/release |
| [v2](v2.md) | proposed | parallel | planned | not implemented |
```

### ADR — binding choice / supersession

```markdown
---
id: ADR-0001
title: Adopt parallel execution
status: proposed
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
related: [DES-0001@v2, EVAL-0001]
supersedes: null
superseded_by: null
---
# ADR-0001 — Adopt parallel execution
## Context and decision drivers
## Decision (specific and actionable)
## Alternatives and rejection reasons
## Consequences / risks / follow-up
## Evidence, owners, implementation links
```

## Quality gates

- No fabricated approval, deployment, benchmark, or implementation claim.
- Every FEAT acceptance criterion is verifiable; every design version says what changed; every ADR includes alternatives and consequences.
- Selected **≠** implemented; rejected/superseded material stays available; indexes and reciprocal supersession references are updated.

# Framework-first architecture document template

Use for `docs/architecture/<system>.md` (living, implemented architecture) or DES versioned snapshots (proposed designs). **Keep evidence-backed descriptions separate from conceptual pseudocode.** Remove sections that genuinely do not apply but retain the framework → object model → runtime explanation order.

---
title: <System> — <Framework> Architecture
status: implemented | partially-implemented | proposed
as_of: YYYY-MM-DD
design: DES-xxxx@vN  # if applicable
related: [FEAT-xxxx, ADR-xxxx, EXP-xxxx]
---
# <System>: <Framework> Architecture

## 1. System at a glance
- **Purpose:**
- **Framework:** <name and authoritative meaning>
- **Architectural style:** <e.g. ports/adapters, layered, plugin-based; only if supported>
- **System boundary:** inside vs outside
- **Current status and evidence:** implemented/documented-only/proposed; code links and as-of date

## 2. Framework model — <Framework Name>
Explain the full framework as a cohesive model *before* details.
- **Contract:** what the framework guarantees and what it intentionally does not.
- **Lifecycle:** how its stages compose from start to finish.

| Stage / letter | Canonical name | Purpose | Input → output | Owner / collaborators | Implementation reference | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <letter> | <verified expansion or Unverified> | ... | ... | ... | ... | verified / documented / unknown |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Entry[Request] --> Stage1[Framework stage 1]
  Stage1 --> Stage2[Framework stage 2]
  Stage2 --> Result[Outcome]
```

## 3. OOP system model
Make a logical OO design explicit even if implementation uses Rust traits/modules or TS functions.
**Tag every row** as ACTUAL (code declaration) or CONCEPTUAL (architecture abstraction).

| Type / role | Actual or conceptual | Responsibility (single owner) | Owned state | Public contract/operations | Collaborators | Code reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HarnessSession | CONCEPTUAL | ... | ... | start(), run(), close() (pseudocode) | ... | not a literal class |

### 3.1 Contracts, invariants, composition
- Interfaces/traits and their purpose; signatures only with code evidence, otherwise pseudocode.
- Who constructs each object; ownership, lifetime and persistence.
- Composition/delegation vs inheritance; extension points and substitution boundaries.
- Failure, security and concurrency invariants.

```mermaid
classDiagram
  class HarnessSession {
    <<conceptual>>
    +run(request) result
    +close()
  }
  class ContextProvider {
    <<conceptual>>
    +buildEntryPoint() context
  }
  HarnessSession --> ContextProvider : requests context
```
> Diagram depicts logical contracts, NOT actual classes, unless verified against source.

## 4. Component boundaries and data ownership
- Runtime host, adapters, user interface, storage, external systems.
- Request/control flow vs data/persistence flow.
- Trust/security/permission boundaries.

## 5. Runtime interactions and state transitions
### 5.1 Main request lifecycle
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant Host
  participant Adapter
  participant Harness
  Client->>Host: submit request
  Host->>Adapter: launch/continue run
  Adapter->>Harness: execute
  Harness-->>Adapter: events/result
  Adapter-->>Host: normalized events
  Host-->>Client: stream/update
```
> Illustrative until real call flow is verified.
### 5.2 Alternative workflows and failures
- Different entrypoints / adapters / execution modes.
- Retries, abort, permissions, context refresh, persistence, cleanup.

## 6. Design rationale
- Why this decomposition; alternatives, trade-offs and constraints.
- Observability, extensibility, safety implications.

## 7. Variants and implementation differences
| Variant | Reused contracts | What changes | Evidence / limitation |
|---|---|---|---|

## 8. Implementation map and current boundaries
| Architectural role | Module / type / function | Verification status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
- Known limitations, disputed and stale claims, missing evidence.

## 9. Evolution and related records
- Selected/current design and effective date.
- DES snapshots, superseding ADRs, measured EXP/EVAL and source references.

### Specific framework and acronym requirements

When a project names a framework, verify its canonical components, labels, and order from authoritative repository documentation and source. Preserve those terms; map each verified stage to documented roles, contracts, state, and implementation. Mark any missing expansion or mapping as unverified; never infer or invent one.

### Fallback without code access

Reorganize existing information under the headings, produce a *conceptual* OOP mapping rather than pretending concrete classes exist, and leave implementation references and acronym expansions as unverified. Do **not** treat claims from a document explicitly labeled stale as present-day implementation evidence.
